transcript.text: Thanks everyone for being here. As we all know, the platform team has a replacement for our shared self-hosted runners based on ephemeral runners, and it passed the standard build-speed and failure-recovery tests in staging. The draft operating policy is on the table: 20 concurrent jobs, 30-day log retention, and notably it doesn't specify immutable log storage or build-provenance attestations. Before I give my final approval, I want to hear from each of you — developer productivity, site reliability, and compliance — on whether this policy is ready to publish or if there are gaps we need to address first. Who wants to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: There's a critical gap in the proposal that I haven't updated yet. Yesterday, while helping the release team debug a separate build, I confirmed that our production release pipeline uses privileged Docker-in-Docker, which cannot run on the proposed ephemeral runner profile. The workable design is exactly two isolated persistent runners dedicated to release jobs, with all remaining jobs going to ephemeral runners. The current proposal doesn't account for this hybrid model at all, and if we publish it as-is, release jobs will fail in production.

transcript.text: During an unrelated queue investigation this morning, I measured a campaign-day burst of 28 simultaneous CI jobs. The safe production ceiling is exactly 32 concurrent jobs, and the queue should generate an alert when it exceeds 24 jobs. For the policy, 32 is the max_concurrent_jobs value to use; 28 is only the observed burst that motivates raising the draft limit. I haven't added these measurements to the capacity dashboard yet.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a compliance gap. While preparing audit evidence this afternoon, I confirmed that build logs for our regulated release repositories must be retained for exactly 180 days in immutable storage, and each production build must produce a signed provenance attestation. The draft policy's 30-day retention with no immutability or provenance requirements falls far short of these requirements. I haven't opened the compliance ticket yet, but these are hard requirements we cannot publish without addressing.
transcript.speaker: A4

commitments.detail: Update the operating policy to reflect the hybrid runner architecture: two isolated persistent runners for release jobs using privileged Docker-in-Docker, with all remaining jobs on ephemeral runners.
Set max_concurrent_jobs to 32 and configure a queue alert threshold at 24 concurrent jobs.
Set log retention to 180 days in immutable storage for regulated release repositories, and require signed provenance attestations for each production build.
Update the proposal to incorporate the hybrid model with two dedicated persistent runners for release jobs.
Add the capacity measurements (32-job ceiling, 24-job alert threshold, 28-job observed burst) to the capacity dashboard.
Open the compliance ticket documenting the 180-day immutable log retention and signed provenance attestation requirements for regulated release repositories.
